svg.aria-label: Upper left: the Sedov-Taylor profiles of density, velocity and pressure against radius for gamma 5/3 and 7/5. Density is piled into a thin shell behind the shock, and pressure levels off at about a third of its post-shock value in the interior. Upper right: Taylor's 25 Trinity points, five halves log radius against log time, lying along a line of slope one. Bottom: the residual of each point from that line. The first point, at 0.10 milliseconds, is far below the scale. The rest fall in three bands whose means decrease with time.
svg.text: The residual from that line: the model behind it refuted
Residuals are from the fixed-slope line through rows 2–25. The band means fall from +0.015 to -0.004 to -0.034;
the step between the outer bands is 7.3 times their combined standard error. The three later bands follow Taylor's authority column, C and D pooled.
